verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 3.8
1. Paṭhamavagga
Mallikāsutta
Sāvatthinidānaṁ.
Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikāya deviyā saddhiṁ uparipāsādavaragato hoti.
verses.english: Now at that time King Pasenadi of Kosala was upstairs in the royal longhouse together with Queen Mallikā.

verses.pali: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikaṁ deviṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the king said to the queen,

verses.pali: “atthi nu kho te, mallike, kocañño attanā piyataro”ti?
verses.english: “Mallikā, is there anyone more dear to you than yourself?”

verses.pali: “Natthi kho me, mahārāja, kocañño attanā piyataro.
Tuyhaṁ pana, mahārāja, atthañño koci attanā piyataro”ti?
verses.english: But is there anyone more dear to you than yourself?”

verses.pali: “Mayhampi kho, mallike, natthañño koci attanā piyataro”ti.
Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo pāsādā orohitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala came downstairs from the stilt longhouse, went to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

verses.pali: “idhāhaṁ, bhante, mallikāya deviyā saddhiṁ uparipāsādavaragato mallikaṁ deviṁ etadavocaṁ:
‘atthi nu kho te, mallike, kocañño attanā piyataro’ti?
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, mallikā devī maṁ etadavoca:
‘natthi kho me, mahārāja, kocañño attanā piyataro.
Tuyhaṁ pana, mahārāja, atthañño koci attanā piyataro’ti?
Evaṁ vuttāhaṁ, bhante, mallikaṁ deviṁ etadavocaṁ:
‘mayhampi kho, mallike, natthañño koci attanā piyataro’”ti.
Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
verses.english: Then, understanding this matter, on that occasion the Buddha spoke this verse:

verses.pali: “Sabbā disā anuparigamma cetasā,
verses.english: “Having explored every quarter with the mind,

verses.pali: Nevajjhagā piyataramattanā kvaci;
verses.english: one finds no-one dearer than oneself.

verses.pali: Evaṁ piyo puthu attā paresaṁ,
verses.english: Likewise for others, each holds themselves dear;

verses.pali: Tasmā na hiṁse paramattakāmo”ti.
verses.english: so one who desires self-knowledge would harm no other.”
